name: Century Aluminum Company
tagline: Global producer of primary aluminum with integrated alumina operations
hero_kpi_rationale: Le projet de nouvelle fonderie en Oklahoma en partenariat avec EGA produira 750 000 tonnes d'aluminium par an, plus que doublant la capacité de production américaine et constituant le premier nouveau projet majeur depuis 1980.

kpis.explanation: Joint development agreement with EGA to construct the first new primary aluminum smelter in the United States since 1980, located in Inola, Oklahoma.
kpis.signal: Major production capacity expansion, first new US smelter in 45 years.
kpis.description: The new smelter in Inola, Oklahoma, being developed with EGA (Century holds 40%, EGA holds 60%), will produce 750,000 tonnes of primary aluminum annually, more than doubling current U.S. production capacity. Construction expected to begin by end of 2026, subject to completion of detailed engineering and power agreements.
kpis._hero_history_unverified_reason: KPI 'New Smelter Project' (Inola) not found with explicit annual production capacity values in tonnes/year for 4+ consecutive years. Documen

kpis.explanation: Average London Metal Exchange price for primary aluminum, a key determinant of revenue.
kpis.signal: Favorable pricing environment supported by low global inventory levels and improving demand.
kpis.description: The average LME aluminum price for 2025 was $2,630 per tonne, up from $2,419 in 2024. Global macroeconomic trends and low inventory levels near all-time lows have created a supportive pricing environment.

kpis.explanation: Regional premium for aluminum sold in the United States, reflecting tariff impact and supply dynamics.
kpis.signal: Significant increase driven by Section 232 aluminum tariff escalations, materially positive for financial results.
kpis.description: The average Midwest Premium for 2025 was $1,295 per tonne, up significantly from $427 in 2024. This substantial increase resulted from the tariff increases implemented in February and May 2025, which increased tariff rates from 10% to 25% to 50%, creating material positive impact on the company's financial position.

kpis.explanation: Total capital spending on fixed assets for maintenance and growth projects.
kpis.signal: Ongoing investment in plant sustainability and operational improvements.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures for 2025 totaled $100.2 million, including maintenance and development projects. For 2026, the company estimates total capital spending of $170-180 million, including approximately $60-70 million for Grundartangi repairs (expected to be insurance-reimbursed), $45 million for Mt. Holly restart, and $25 million for Jamalco investments.

kpis.explanation: Completed divestiture of Hawesville, Kentucky facility to finance domestic aluminum production expansion.
kpis.signal: Strategic asset sale generating capital for new smelter project and Mt. Holly potline restart.
kpis.description: On February 2, 2026, the company completed the sale of its Hawesville, Kentucky facility to a Terawulf affiliate for $200.0 million in cash plus a 6.8% non-dilutive minority equity interest in the Terawulf data center development. Proceeds are intended to finance the restart of Mt. Holly's last potline and investments in the new Inola smelter project.

kpis.name_en: IRA Section 45X Advanced Manufacturing Tax Credit
kpis.explanation: Advanced manufacturing production tax credit of 10% on eligible domestic aluminum production costs under Inflation Reduction Act.
kpis.signal: Government incentive reducing production costs for domestically produced aluminum through 2033 (reduced 25% annually beginning 2031).
kpis.description: Final regulations for Section 45X were issued on October 24, 2024. The company has recognized a receivable and corresponding offset to COGS and SG&A expenses for the 10% tax credit on eligible domestic production costs. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4, 2025, requires annual reductions of 25% beginning in 2031, phasing out to zero by 2034.

kpis.name_en: Jamalco 55% Interest Acquisition Bargain Purchase Gain
kpis.explanation: Non-recurring gain from acquisition of 55% interest in Jamalco joint venture with Jamaica government.
kpis.signal: Strategic acquisition providing vertical integration of alumina supply with ~1.4 million tonnes annual capacity.
kpis.description: On May 2, 2023, the company acquired a 55% interest in Jamalco (Jamaica alumina refinery) through acquisition of General Alumina Holdings Limited. A bargain purchase gain of $245.9 million was recognized in 2024. Jamalco has approximately 1.4 million tonnes of alumina production capacity, with the company acting as managing partner and consuming the commensurate alumina off-take.

kpis.signal: Total des actifs de 2.27 Mds € dernière année
kpis.description: Total des actifs extrait yfinance sur les 4 dernières années.
kpis.explanation_en: Total Assets, sum of all assets on the balance sheet.

stories_kpis.explanation: Expected resumption of production on Grundartangi potline idled due to transformer failures in September-October 2025.
stories_kpis.signal: Resolution of major production disruption, restoring approximately two-thirds of Grundartangi capacity.
stories_kpis.description: In October 2025, Grundartangi smelter's potline was temporarily idled due to transformer failures in September-October 2025, reducing production by approximately two-thirds. The other potline remains in full production. Production resumption is estimated to begin by end of April 2026. Losses are expected to be covered under insurance policies.

stories_kpis.name_fr: Subvention du Département américain de l'Énergie
stories_kpis.name_en: US Department of Energy Cooperative Agreement Award
stories_kpis.explanation: Federal funding award for construction of new aluminum smelter under Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act.
stories_kpis.signal: Significant government support for domestic aluminum production strategic initiative.
stories_kpis.description: On January 10, 2025, the company entered into a Cooperative Agreement with the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations for up to $500 million in Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act funding to build the new aluminum smelter in Inola, Oklahoma as part of the Industrial Demonstrations Program.

ai_positioning.summary: Century Aluminum does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filings. The company's data center minority interest through the Hawesville sale relates to high-performance computing infrastructure but is not positioned as an AI initiative.
ai_positioning.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

risks.title: Aluminum Price Fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: Position in MD&A, impact on revenues, explicit discussion of pricing components and volatility (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Fluctuations in LME base prices and regional premiums can significantly impact revenue and profitability.

risks.title: Electrical Power Cost and Supply Risk
risks.score_rationale: Position in Risk Factors and MD&A, power represents >84% of COGS, market-based pricing exposure, transmission risks (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Power cost fluctuations, grid stability issues, and supply disruptions could materially impact production and profitability. Annual cost sensitivity of $15.9M per $1/MWh.

risks.title: Foreign Currency Risk
risks.score_rationale: Exposure to ISK, EUR, CNY, JMD through operations in Iceland, Netherlands, China, Jamaica (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Fluctuations in USD relative to Iceland krona, Euro, Chinese renminbi and Jamaican dollar impact labor costs, maintenance, and anode procurement.

risks.title: Regulatory and Environmental Compliance Risk
risks.score_rationale: Discussion of evolving environmental regulations and tariff policy changes (Section 232 changes in 2025) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Changes to environmental regulations, tariff policies, and critical minerals provisions under IRA Section 45X could materially affect operations and tax benefits.

risks.title: Project Development and Execution Risk
risks.score_rationale: New smelter project subject to numerous contingencies: detailed engineering, power agreements, definitive JV agreement, construction timeline (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The new Inola smelter joint venture is subject to completion of engineering, negotiation of long-term power agreements with PSO, and definitive JV agreement with EGA.

risks.title: Equipment Failure and Production Disruption Risk
risks.score_rationale: Recent Grundartangi transformer failures caused two-thirds production reduction; Jamalco equipment failure in 2023 resulted in $30.4M margin impact (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Equipment failures can disrupt production and impact financial results. Grundartangi potline expected offline through April 2026 due to transformer failures.

risks.title: Litigation Risk
risks.score_rationale: Multiple ongoing legal actions noted but assessed as immaterial individually and in aggregate (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company is defendant in several legal actions but believes none will have material adverse effect individually or in aggregate.

risks.title: Credit and Liquidity Risk
risks.score_rationale: Debt obligations and contractual commitments including long-term power contracts extending through 2036 (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Debt servicing and contractual obligations for power supply, alumina, labor agreements and retiree benefits could affect liquidity.
